posts.title: Beyond Linux: A Journey Through the Open Source Ecosystem
posts.description: What follows is the text of the talk I gave at Linux Day 2026 in Modena, lightly adapted for the blog. The talk was in Italian, in front of a Linux audience - which explains a few of the jokes. Linux is one of the best-known players in the open source world, but it's not the only possible path. posts.title: SmartOS: The illumos Way of Thinking About Servers
posts.description: As I often say, I like simplicity and predictability. My servers are generally built around that principle: the server itself (physical or virtual) is just a coordinator of containers. When it's based on FreeBSD, those containers take the form of jails and VMs. In case of disaster, restoring is simple, and I talked about it at EuroBSDCon 2026 in Brussels . posts.title: Aggressive caching for a Mastodon reverse proxy: what to cache, what to never cache, and why content negotiation will eventually betray you
posts.description: I have written before about putting a cache in front of snac , and more recently about the HAProxy layer in front of FediMeteo . The general idea is always the same: the reverse proxy should absorb the repetitive, public work that has no business reaching the application server.
